oewn-00029763-r.learner: used when you are adding another piece of information to what you have already said.
examples: The journey would, moreover, give her a peep at Jane.
Mrs. Collins's pretty friend had, moreover, caught his fancy very much.

oewn-13276044-n.learner: the money that comes to you, whether you work for it or not, over a set length of time.
examples: The Miss Webbs all play, and their father has not so good an income as yours.
Mr. and Mrs. Collins have a comfortable income, but not such a one as will allow of frequent journeys.

oewn-13834819-n.learner: the fact of being connected to someone by blood, by marriage, or by adoption.
examples: I feel myself called upon, by our relationship, and my situation in life, to condole with you.
Elizabeth honestly and heartily expressed her delight in the prospect of their relationship.

oewn-13802931-n.learner: the way two or more people stand towards each other.
examples: The relationship between a teacher and her pupils changes over the years.

oewn-13951421-n.learner: a state in which people are joined to each other, above all in what they feel.
examples: Their relationship grew closer after her illness.

oewn-00010428-v.learner: to act in a certain way, or to carry yourself in a certain way.
examples: what can have induced him to behave so cruelly?
I should like to know how he behaves among strangers.

oewn-02525332-v.learner: to act in a good and proper way.
examples: Their mother told them to behave while she was out of the room.

oewn-14474157-n.learner: the state of being needed and impossible to do without.
examples: she felt the necessity of appearing more like herself.
he voluntarily acknowledged that the necessity of his absence had been self-imposed.

oewn-09390100-n.learner: anything that you cannot do without.
examples: Warm clothing was a necessity in that cold country.

oewn-01818782-v.learner: to give someone strength in their spirits or their feelings.
examples: Charlotte tried to console her.
Nothing could console and nothing appease her.

oewn-02380222-v.learner: to carry out an activity or take part in it; to be busy with it.
examples: his excessive distress will not allow him to pursue any measure in the best and safest way
She then proceeded to inquire into the measures which her father had intended to pursue.

oewn-02004900-v.learner: to follow something, either chasing it or moving along it as if chasing.
examples: Pursuing her way along the lane, she then began it.
they pursued the accustomed circuit

oewn-02381520-v.learner: to take something further, or to move it forward.
examples: The subject was pursued no further, and the gentlemen soon afterwards went away.

oewn-00095870-r.learner: from a higher level or position to a lower one, either in real space or in a way we only picture.
examples: she sat down, resolving within herself to draw no limits in future to the impudence of an impudent man
when persons sit down to a card table they must take their chance of these things

oewn-00096162-r.learner: away from a place that is more central, or away from a place further north.
examples: He came down to see the place
Miss Darcy is always down for the summer months.

oewn-00096639-r.learner: so that something becomes weaker or less strong.
examples: He turned the lamp down until the room was almost dark.

oewn-04864314-n.learner: a strength of spirit that lets you meet danger or pain without showing fear.
examples: Elizabeth's courage did not fail her.

oewn-08455525-n.learner: the trees and other plants growing together in a large area thick with trees.

oewn-15122728-n.learner: the hard, tough material that lies under the bark of a tree.

oewn-04605909-n.learner: any instrument that you blow into that is not one of the brass instruments.
